rule_pairs.difference: MF: EM-GRD >= 07, tested only in FLEASGN-PREMAP and bypassable by re-keying the id because FLEASGN-ENTER has no grade test; DE: grade >= fleet_rule.min_grade (6) tested in checkEmployee, and step 2/3 are only rendered after it passes. Same grade numbers are used for the 15 transferees on both sides although the thresholds differ (07 vs 6).

MF: skips T duplicates in storage order, X (transferred) passes as current, ENTER paths have no not-found exit; DE: employee_no is unique, request requires status A, statement/assignment pages accept any status (no trim/upper-case).

rule_pairs.topic: Rehire duplicates / one record per employment
rule_pairs.difference: MF keeps one EMPLOYEE occurrence per employment (CALC DUPLICATES LAST; 2 ids in the unload have a T and an A occurrence) and pays each occurrence separately keyed by db-key; DE employee_no is UNIQUE so a rehire reuses one row.
MF keys an existing VH-VEHID (no vehicle maintenance in source); DE picks from the computed pool list or registers a new car (plate normalised, make/model/price/CO2 required) inside the request.

MF: "held" = EMP-VEHICLE member; PL pool loans never connect, so a car out on pool loan can be assigned again; DE: available = owner null AND no open assignment, checked at step 1 only (no re-check at submit, no DB constraint).
MF has no check (20 unload employees hold two open cars); DE refuses a request when an open assignment exists (0 seed employees with two open).
AS-RSN NC/RP/PL (default NC, unchecked) has no portal equivalent; portal records car_request status DELIVERED instead.
Both accept any start date without plausibility checks; MF requires a keyed YYYYMMDD (digits only), DE defaults to today in dd.MM.yyyy.
MF AS-ASGID = A + session counter (never read); DE uses BIGSERIAL ids.

rule_pairs.topic: Car request record delivered at once
rule_pairs.difference: DE writes car_request DELIVERED plus the assignment and vehicle owner in one transaction; MF stores only the ASSIGNMENT (and EMP-VEHICLE connect).

rule_pairs.topic: Current car shown to the user
rule_pairs.difference: MF inquiry shows the latest-starting assignment even if returned; DE shows the first open assignment (start desc) and full history.

MF: list x VH-BPCT (per-vehicle annual %) / 1200 - EM-CNTRB, GBP; inquiry ROUNDED full month, batch prorated by car days and TRUNCATED, floored at 0. DE: list x 1% + list x 0.03% x commute_km per month, EUR, prorated by days/monthDays HALF_UP per line, no contribution, no floor, current list price and commute_km.

MF period dates come from the BENEFIT-PERIOD record (BP-STRT..BP-END); car days capped by AS-END and EM-LEAV. DE period = calendar month of yyyy-MM (default previous month), days capped by end_date only.

rule_pairs.topic: Which assignments are taxed in a period
rule_pairs.difference: MF taxes only the latest-starting assignment that started on or before period end (any reason incl. PL, any grade/status); DE sums a line for every assignment overlapping the month.
MF skips occurrences not employed in the period, caps car days at EM-LEAV and flags L; DE never reads hire_date/leave_date and has no leaver flag.

rule_pairs.topic: Benefit output, control totals and payroll hand-off
rule_pairs.difference: MF writes BENOUT per period (new dataset, abort RC16 skips count and FTP); DE renders the statement only and persists nothing.
MF has BENEFIT-PERIOD records with O/C status (claims only into the open current period; run takes a parm period, status not checked); DE has no period entity and recomputes any month on every view.
MF: journey date must be inside the open current period; DE: claim date defaults to today with no check (any past or future date).
Both require a positive whole number; MF miles 1-99999 (map PIC 9(5)), DE km > 0 with no upper bound.

MF: amount not stored; batch recomputes miles x BP-MRATE (0.445 GBP/mile in all 13 periods) ROUNDED per claim at run time. DE: amount frozen at submit = km x 0.305 EUR/km HALF_EVEN, statement sums stored amounts.
MF stores MC-VEHID of the latest assignment (643 of 1511 unload claims have one); DE mileage_claim has no vehicle column.
Both store new claims as pending (P / SUBMITTED) and pay only approved (A / APPROVED); neither source has an approval step. Codes differ: A/P/R vs APPROVED/SUBMITTED/REJECTED.
DE lists the last 6 months of claims; MF has no claim inquiry.
MF keys vehicle id and takes the last-stored VEH-ASSIGN member (ALREADY RETURNED if ended); DE looks up exact case-sensitive plate and any open assignment.
Both reject a return date before the start, allow same day and future; MF YYYYMMDD keyed, DE defaults to today.
Both close the assignment and release the car (EMP-VEHICLE disconnect / owner null); DE also stores a car_return row.
MF map captures WK-ODO but never processes it; DE requires and stores odometer_km.
MF FLERETN has no menu route; DE return page is in the top navigation.
MF menu options 1/2/3/X and PF3 back to menu; DE top-nav links on every page plus a 3-step wizard with Zurueck.
DE searches number/name contains, max 50; MF only exact id lookup.
MF: mileage rate per BENEFIT-PERIOD (BP-MRATE) and benefit % per VEHICLE (VH-BPCT); DE: one fleet_rule row DE (min_grade, benefit_pct, commute_pct, mileage_rate) read by literal.

rule_pairs.topic: Mandatory ownership of assignments and claims
rule_pairs.difference: Portal has no rule id but the same constraint as NOT NULL FKs (assignment.employee_id/vehicle_id, mileage_claim.employee_id).

rule_pairs.topic: Mileage claim by a leaver / inactive employee
rule_pairs.difference: Shared: neither side applies an active-status or leave-date eligibility rejection before accepting a mileage claim. Portal find/submit accepts any found employee with positive kilometres; FleetService adds no status or leave-date guard. Mainframe-only: FLEMILE-PREMAP and FLEMILE-ENTER inspect EM-STAT and repeatedly OBTAIN DUPLICATE EMPLOYEE while it is T, rather than rejecting a leaver. ENTER checks not-found only before that loop; neither loop has an explicit not-found/end-of-duplicates exit. An all-T employee id therefore has a no-exit loop risk if the exhausted lookup leaves EM-STAT at T, not a guaranteed accepted claim. Once the loop finishes, ENTER checks journey date and miles, but not EM-LEAV or active status, before storing the claim.

shared_data.differences: Period-scoped rates and close status only on MF; single static rule only on DE.

callers.finding: JCL FLEBEN01: STEP010 runs PGM=FLEBEN01 with SYSIN period &PERIOD; STEP020 ICETOOL count and STEP030 FTP payroll run only if RC <= 4. Schedule (WD+3 after close) exists only as a comment; the FTP deck is outside the repo.

FLEMENU routes 1->FLEEMPI, 2->FLEASGN, 3->FLEMILE, X/PF3/CLEAR leave; every function PF3s back to FLEMENU. FLERETN has no caller, so its PF3 back-edge in FLEMENU.reached_from is dead; the worker marks FLERETN unreached correctly.
FLEUNLD is a standalone job (IDMSBCF unload + ICETOOL counts); nothing in the repo schedules it; it is the hand-over data source.
No source maintains EMPLOYEE, VEHICLE or BENEFIT-PERIOD or sets MC-STAT A/R, yet the unload holds approved claims and closed periods: those callers are outside the repo.

Portal entry is the welcome-file employees.xhtml; top-nav links employees/request/mileage/return on every page; statement and assignment are reached only from employee rows (and assignment from the wizard redirect).
mileage.xhtml?employee= and return.xhtml?plate= viewParams have no in-app caller (only a typed URL), as the worker says.
/health servlet is called by the k8s readiness/liveness probes and gf-tenant.sh wait_https; seed load is the only batch-like job.

Caller asymmetry: MF benefit is a batch run per closed period (FLEBEN01) plus an on-screen monthly figure (FLEEMPI); DE has only on-page computation (statement f:viewAction -> StatementBean.load), nothing persisted and no payroll hand-off. Neither side calls the other.

surprises: The 15 transferees keep the same employee number in both countries; their MF occurrence is status X with EM-LEAV = portal hire_date - 1 day, and they have no MF assignments, claims or BENOUT records. The id string is the only link, and industries/manufacturing/global-fleet/ESTATE.md:31 gives the wrong prefixes for both sides (MF E101 plus E1009; DE E204 plus E1009).

The MF dialogs treat X like A, so FLEASGN could give a transferee a UK car while the portal holds an open DE assignment for them (10 of the 15 do): the two estates together allow two company cars per person.
Neither estate has a mileage approval path, yet both pay only approved claims (MF 1313 A / 129 P; DE 609 APPROVED / 60 SUBMITTED). Claims keyed in either UI are never paid by any code in the repo.

Benefit maths differs on every axis: per-vehicle annual % /12 minus contribution, truncated, one car per period, capped at leaving date (MF batch) vs 1% + 0.03%/commute-km, HALF_UP, every overlapping car, no leave cap (DE). The MF inquiry screen rounds a full month, so even within MF the screen and payroll differ.
Mileage money is recomputed at run time from the period rate on MF (ROUNDED) but frozen at submission on DE (HALF_EVEN); rate changes affect MF history but not DE.
Holder integrity is the opposite way round: MF unload has 20 employees with two open cars and PL loans bypass the held check; DE seed has none, but its pool check is not repeated at submit.

Entry "deploy/gf-tenant.sh (lines 292-325, 409-429)" is not a plain path.

applied_corrections.correction: Add rule: "Mileage claim for any found employee": MileageBean.find/submit require only employee != null and km > 0; no status, leave_date, grade or car check. Status observed.

rule_pairs.topic: Grade eligibility for a company car
rule_pairs.difference: Both compare a numeric grade to a threshold and both use the same grade scale (the 15 shared people have the same grade on both sides). The mainframe threshold is 07, hard-coded in FLEASGN-PREMAP only; FLEASGN-ENTER does not re-check it, and 9 stored assignments belong to grade 05/06 employees. The portal reads min_grade 6 from fleet_rule and checks it in wizard step 1 only.

rule_pairs.topic: Requester must be on file and current
rule_pairs.difference: Mainframe: unknown id gives 'EMPLOYEE NOT ON FILE'; occurrences with status T are skipped and X (transferred abroad) counts as current. Portal: employee_no is unique, an exact match is required after trim and upper-casing, and the status must be 'A'. The portal has no X status and no duplicate occurrences.
Both refuse a blank id: the mainframe with a message in FLEEMPI-ENTER and FLEASGN-PREMAP, the portal with required=true on the wizard input. Only the message text differs.

Mainframe: any vehicle id on file that is not an EMP-VEHICLE member, so a car out on pool loan (PL) can be assigned again. Portal: a pool car is offered only if owner is null AND it has no open assignment; the list is taken once in step 1 and not re-checked at submit.
The portal refuses a second open assignment. The mainframe has no such check, and 20 employees in the unload hold 2 open assignments.
AS-RSN NC/RP/PL exists only on the mainframe, and PL does not link the car as held. The portal's 'pool' choice is a permanent assignment of an unowned car, not a loan; the portal has no reason code.

Neither checks the date against hire date, leaving date or other assignments. The mainframe date is keyed, required and 9(8) digits only, so an invalid calendar date passes. The portal defaults to today in dd.MM.yyyy through the JSF date converter.
Mainframe: 'A' + a 9-digit counter from the session work record, never read. Portal: assignment.id BIGSERIAL, not shown to users.

rule_pairs.topic: Register a newly delivered car / request record
rule_pairs.difference: The portal wizard creates vehicle rows and a car_request with status DELIVERED. No mainframe source in the repo STOREs a VEHICLE; vehicles are maintained outside the repo.

rule_pairs.topic: Current car shown for an employee
rule_pairs.difference: Mainframe inquiry shows the latest-starting assignment even if it was returned. Portal shows the first assignment with a null end_date in start-date-descending order, so a returned car is never shown as current.

Mainframe: list x per-vehicle VH-BPCT / 1200 (annual % over 12 months) minus the employee contribution EM-CNTRB, floored at 0, in GBP. Portal: list x fleet_rule.benefit_pct/100 (1% a month) + list x commute_pct/100 x commute_km, with no contribution and no per-vehicle %, in EUR. The portal has no commute part on the mainframe side, and the mainframe has no per-vehicle % on the portal side.

FLEBEN01 prorates by car days / period days and TRUNCATES. All 857 holdout BENOUT records with days>0 match truncation; 415 would differ under half-up rounding. FLEEMPI shows an unprorated ROUNDED month. The portal prorates by days / calendar-month days with HALF_UP per line and sums the rounded lines.

Both use inclusive day counts from max(start, period start) to min(end, period end). The mainframe also caps at the employee's leaving date EM-LEAV and uses BP-STRT/BP-END from the period record. The portal never reads leave_date and uses the calendar month.

rule_pairs.topic: Which assignments are taxed in a period
rule_pairs.difference: FLEBEN01 taxes only the latest-starting assignment that starts on or before period end, regardless of reason, grade or status. The portal statement produces one line for EVERY assignment overlapping the month, so a mid-month replacement is taxed on both cars there but only on the later one on the mainframe.

rule_pairs.topic: Who is included in a benefit computation
rule_pairs.difference: Mainframe: area sweep of every EMPLOYEE occurrence hired on or before period end and not left before period start; one BENOUT per occurrence, written only if car days>0 or approved miles>0. Portal: one employee on demand by exact employee_no, any status, with no hire or leave filter and always rendered.

Mainframe caps car days at EM-LEAV and flags L. The portal only blocks status<>'A' in the request wizard; the statement and the other pages ignore leave_date. The portal worker has no rule for this (see corrections).

Mainframe: miles x BP-MRATE (0.445 GBP/mile in all 13 periods) ROUNDED (half-up) per claim at batch time; the online amount is display-only. Portal: km x fleet_rule.mileage_rate (0.305 EUR/km) HALF_EVEN, frozen on the claim at submission, so a later rate change does not reprice it.
Both refuse zero. Units differ: whole miles 9(5) (max 99999) on the mainframe, Integer km with no upper bound on the portal.
The mainframe requires an open current-month BENEFIT-PERIOD and a journey date inside it. The portal accepts any claim date (default today) and has no period entity.

Both store a new claim as not yet approved: 'P' on the mainframe, 'SUBMITTED' on the portal. Neither side has source that sets approved or rejected, although both data sets contain them (MF A 1313 / R 69; portal APPROVED 609 / REJECTED 30).
MC-VEHID takes the latest assignment's vehicle (868 of 1511 claims have none). mileage_claim on the portal has no vehicle column.

rule_pairs.topic: Only approved claims are paid / shown
rule_pairs.difference: Both count only approved claims dated within the period/month. The difference is in the amount (see the mileage reimbursement pair): recomputed at batch time on the mainframe, the stored amount on the portal.
The portal lists the last 6 months of claims. The mainframe has no claim inquiry screen.

Mainframe: by vehicle id; takes the LAST stored VEH-ASSIGN member (insertion order) and refuses if it has ended. Portal: by exact case-sensitive plate; queries an assignment with a null end_date (any of them).
Both require return date >= start date and allow a same-day return or a future date; the return date becomes the assignment end date.
Mainframe DISCONNECTs from EMP-VEHICLE if it is a member; the portal sets vehicle.owner to null. Both commit in one unit of work.
Mainframe asks for WK-ODO and discards it. The portal requires it and stores it in car_return.odometer_km together with a condition note.
FLERETN has no menu route. The portal return page is on the top navigation of every page.
Mainframe: menu options 1/2/3/X and PF3 back to the menu. Portal: top-nav GET links plus employees -> assignment/statement links and a 3-step wizard with Back.

Mainframe: a batch run per parm-card period, one catalogued dataset per period, and no status check although the header says 'closed'. Portal: computed on every view for any yyyy-MM (default previous month) with nothing stored, so past months recompute.
BENRPT control totals and RC 16 abort with downstream step skip (COND=(4,LT)). The portal shows per-employee totals only and has no payroll hand-off.

Mainframe: unique VH-VEHID and BP-PERIOD; EM-EMPID may repeat (2 rehires: E1010398, E1010524). Portal: employee_no UNIQUE, plate UNIQUE, surrogate BIGSERIAL keys, and one fleet_rule row keyed by country.

Mainframe: assignment must belong to an employee and a vehicle, and a claim to an employee (mandatory automatic). The portal has equivalent NOT NULL FKs, but the vehicle owner is an application-maintained mirror of the open assignment rather than a set.

Portal: one fleet_rule row 'DE' (min grade, %s, rate; currency never read). Mainframe: grade threshold hard-coded 07, benefit % per vehicle (VH-BPCT), mileage rate per period (BP-MRATE); no country table.
The portal searches with a contains match over number and names. The mainframe has exact CALC lookup by id only.

shared_data.mainframe: ASSIGNMENT VIA EMP-ASSIGN (sorted AS-STRT desc) and VEH-ASSIGN (insertion order); AS-ASGID 'A'+9 digits; AS-STRT/AS-END YYYYMMDD with 0 = open; AS-RSN NC/RP/PL. 119 rows, 101 open; reasons NC 83 / RP 27 / PL 9.

shared_data.mainframe: MILEAGE-CLAIM VIA EMP-CLAIM (sorted MC-DATE asc) plus optional PERIOD-CLAIM; MC-CLMID 'C'+9; MC-VEHID; MC-DATE; MC-MILES 9(5) miles; MC-STAT A/P/R; MC-PURP X(10); no amount stored. 1511 claims: A 1313 / P 129 / R 69.

shared_data.mainframe: BENEFIT-PERIOD CALC BP-PERIOD YYYYMM; BP-STRT/BP-END; BP-MRATE 9V999 GBP/mile (0.445 in all 13 periods); BP-STAT O/C (202510-202609 closed with BP-RUNDT on the 3rd of the next month, 202610 open); grade threshold hard-coded.

shared_data.differences: The mainframe parameterises the rate by period and the benefit % by vehicle; the portal parameterises everything by country. Only the mainframe has open/closed periods and a run date.

shared_data.mainframe: BENOUT FB64 per employee occurrence per period (BO-DAYS, BO-TAXB, BO-MILES, BO-MREIM, BO-FLAG) plus the BENRPT control report, FTP'd to payroll.

shared_data.mainframe: None: no request record; FLERETN modifies AS-END only and the odometer is discarded.

callers.finding: Mainframe chain: FLEMENU option 1/2/3 -> FLEEMPI/FLEASGN/FLEMILE (TRANSFER NOFINISH); each PF3 -> FLEMENU. FLERETN has no caller in source, so neither online return nor any reachable path ends an assignment. The workers agree (MF unreached / MF-R25).

Mainframe batch: JCL FLEBEN01 STEP010 PGM=FLEBEN01 (period from SET PERIOD via SYSIN) -> STEP020 ICETOOL count -> STEP030 FTP to payroll (deck not in repo); steps 2-3 have COND=(4,LT), so RC 16 skips them. FLEUNLD is a separate IDMSBCF unload. The portal has no batch caller at all; the benefit is computed by statement.xhtml -> StatementBean.load (f:viewAction) on every GET.

Portal chain: welcome-file employees.xhtml; the layout top-nav reaches employees/request/mileage/return; employees -> assignment and statement via h:link with ?employee; request.submit redirects to assignment. statement is NOT on the top-nav (reached only from employees or a direct URL). /health servlet is reached by k8s probes (gf-tenant.sh deploy_app with /health). Pages call beans, which call FleetService, which uses JPA. Worker inventory is correct.

Callers one side has and the other lacks. Portal only: registering a new vehicle (wizard 'new'), employee search, claim history, a reachable return. Mainframe only: batch benefit run + payroll FTP, period open/close data, flat-file unload. Neither side has a caller for approving claims or maintaining employees (and on the mainframe, vehicles and periods), although both data sets contain approved/rejected claims.

Mileage pricing caller differs. Mainframe: FLEMILE shows a display-only amount and FLEBEN01 2200-MILEAGE recomputes the payable amount per approved claim with the period rate. Portal: MileageBean.submit -> FleetService.submitClaim stores the amount once, and StatementBean only sums the stored amounts.

surprises: The 15 shared people have the same employee number in both countries (E1009100-E1009142). On the mainframe they are status X with EM-LEAV exactly one day before their portal hire_date. Nothing else links the two records, and industries/manufacturing/global-fleet/ESTATE.md:31's prefixes are wrong for both sides.

The holdout data confirms FLEBEN01 truncates: all 857 BENOUT records with days>0 across the 12 periods equal the truncated (VH-LIST*VH-BPCT/1200-EM-CNTRB)*days/mdays; half-up rounding would change 415 of them.

The two benefit formulas share no parameters. GB: annual per-vehicle % /12 minus employee contribution, one car per period, truncated. DE: 1% a month plus 0.03% per commute km, every overlapping car, HALF_UP. Mileage rounding: GB half-up at batch time with the period rate; DE HALF_EVEN frozen at submit.
Neither estate contains the code that approves mileage claims, yet both data sets are mostly approved (MF 1313/1511, portal 609/699) and both pay only approved claims.

The portal statement taxes every overlapping assignment and ignores leave_date. FLEBEN01 taxes only the latest-starting one and caps at EM-LEAV. A mid-month car swap or a leaver gives different days on the two sides.

The mainframe holds 2 open assignments for 20 employees and 9 assignments for grade<07 employees. The portal seed has neither (80 open = 80 owned, no grade<6 holder), so a merged dataset will break the portal's one-car invariant.
